chapter: Society work, Camilla Todd and Storyville
title: Camilla Todd's singing, 1913-25
summary: Todd sang in a straight style with the band, years before Bessie Smith.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Yeah. How often did you have vocalists performing with your group outside of your instrumentals?
Well Miss Todd, she used to sing. She did. Oh yeah.
But only people in the band sang, not extra. No, not, there's not one. You wouldn't hire an extra. Only one. Yeah, but I mean you wouldn't hire an extra man or an extra woman to sing.

No, no. The only time we had that is when we was playing that Tom Anderson on Rampart and Canal. You remember Tom Anderson was the fellow who had all those big houses there in the district they used to call it.
Did Miss Todd accompany herself while she played and sang, or did you other instruments count?
She played in a comedy herself. She played, well we all played in there with her, you see.
Well tell me, did she sing in what we today would call the jazzy or bluesy style, or was it pretty straight?
Well it was pretty straight. But you know she could always make the people like it somehow or other.
Well this was years before Bessie Smith came along, wasn't it? Bessie Smith, let's see, was what she was... What year was that she was? Flourishing around 1926, 1926.
Oh, that was after us. That was after our time.
When was this that Miss Todd was singing?
All the way from 1913 to 1925. And that was a good ten to twelve years before Bessie was
alive. That's right, from 1913. She didn't sing blues? Well, huh? Or did she?
